name: Whey/creatine bulking for neck

lead: Looksmaxxers combine neck training with a calorie surplus, whey protein and creatine monohydrate to build a thicker neck, which they say gives the jaw and frame a stronger look.

Creatine raises muscle phosphocreatine stores and is reported to support high-intensity training capacity and, with resistance training, lean mass; early weight gain is largely water held in muscle. Protein supplements provide dietary protein for muscle repair. These findings concern skeletal muscle in general, and no human study has measured effects on neck size specifically.

paras: People eat in a calorie surplus, take whey and creatine daily, and train the neck directly with resistance a few times per week. Muscle gain builds over months, with creatine's early scale-weight rise mostly water.

A position stand cited on Wikipedia describes creatine as safe for healthy people, and a National Kidney Foundation review found creatinine rises within normal limits. Safety data are lacking for children and pregnancy, and supplement contamination has been reported in some surveys.

angle.text: A calorie surplus with whey and creatine supports the muscle gain from direct neck exercises, which adds neck size and a stronger-looking frame and jaw area. Creatine and protein are among the most studied muscle-building supplements, though not for the neck specifically.

lead: Whey and creatine bulking for the neck refers to the practice of combining a calorie surplus, whey protein and creatine monohydrate with direct neck exercises, with the aim of increasing neck muscle size. In looksmaxxing communities a thicker neck is often discussed as contributing to a stronger-looking frame and jaw area.

Creatine is the most widely studied sports supplement. Reviews report that it improves performance in short, high-intensity exercise and, combined with resistance training, can increase lean mass.[1] These findings concern skeletal muscle in general; no published human study has measured the effect of whey or creatine on neck size specifically.
infobox: Calorie surplus, protein powder, creatine monohydrate, neck exercises

paras: The practice combines three elements discussed on forums: eating above maintenance calories, taking supplemental protein such as whey, and taking creatine monohydrate, alongside neck-specific resistance work. Practitioners describe the neck as a muscle group that responds to training like other muscles.

Creatine is an organic compound that helps regenerate ATP, with about 95% of the body's stores in skeletal muscle. Supplementation is reported to raise muscle phosphocreatine by roughly 20 to 40 percent and to improve repeated high-intensity work, with no significant effect on aerobic endurance.[1]

A 2018 review in the Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition described creatine monohydrate as the most effective supplement for increasing high-intensity exercise capacity and muscle mass during training.[1] Early weight gain, usually in the first week, is mainly water retained in muscle.[1]

A position stand summarized on Wikipedia describes creatine as safe for healthy people, and a 2019 National Kidney Foundation review of 15 studies found creatinine levels that rose slightly but stayed within normal limits, with no evidence of kidney damage; three case reports described possible renal effects.[1] Safety data are lacking for children and pregnancy.[1] A 2011 survey of 33 Italian supplements found over half exceeded European limits for at least one contaminant.[1]

No studies found. No published trial has examined whey protein or creatine for increasing neck size or neck appearance. Research on creatine in resistance-trained and older adults concerns muscle mass and strength generally, as summarized above.[1]

lore.intro: The practice is discussed in looksmaxxing communities as part of building a wider neck, though no forum material was available to cite here.

claims.claim: Supplements and a calorie surplus will thicken the neck.
